ao.headline: Angola hosts AU summit to adopt new conflict prevention strategy
ao.dek: Angola will host the African Union's first extraordinary summit on conflict prevention and resolution, aiming to shift from reactive to proactive crisis management.
paragraphs: The African Union will hold its first extraordinary summit on conflict prevention, management, and resolution in Luanda, Angola, on August twenty-ninth and thirtieth. This marks the first time since the AU's founding that heads of state will convene specifically on this issue, according to Miguel Bembe, Angola's ambassador to Ethiopia and spokesperson for the conference.

The summit's central objective is to transition from a reactive stance to a proactive, structural strategy for crisis prevention across the continent. Bembe stated that the meeting will conclude with the adoption of the Luanda Decision, complemented by Action Plans and an Implementation Matrix, which will clearly define objectives, targets, indicators, responsible parties, budgeting, and deadlines.

Bembe highlighted that these three documents represent an innovation, as previous extraordinary conferences typically adopted only a Political Declaration and a Decision. Angola proposed this new approach to ensure concrete results, with specific deadlines and monitoring mechanisms for implementation, addressing current challenges like weak coordination and underutilized operational structures.

ao.headline: BFA establishes direct link with Citibank for global financial operations
ao.dek: Banco de Fomento Angola (BFA) announced a new relationship with Citibank, enabling direct international payments and strengthening Angola's connection to global financial centers.
paragraphs: The BFA has become the first Angolan bank to establish a direct operational link with Citibank, one of the largest financial institutions globally. This move, described by BFA as a "historic milestone," aims to enhance its capacity to support clients, businesses, and investors in international transactions.

This new relationship will allow Citibank to provide its infrastructure and international network to process BFA operations. This will facilitate financial flows for BFA clients between Angola, the United States, and other parts of the world, according to a BFA statement.

The BFA views this connection as a significant sign of confidence in its stability, governance, risk control, and compliance with international financial standards. The bank stated that this reinforces its ambition to play a more relevant role in linking the Angolan economy with major international financial hubs.

km.headline: Mayotte woman kills 24-year-old man with machete in domestic dispute
km.dek: A 22-year-old Malagasy woman is in police custody after allegedly killing her 24-year-old partner with a machete in Koungou, Mayotte, during a domestic dispute.
paragraphs: A 24-year-old man died on Wednesday afternoon in Koungou, Mayotte, after sustaining multiple machete wounds at his home in the Plateau neighborhood. The incident, reported by Mayotte La 1ère, occurred around one thirty in the afternoon following a violent argument within the couple.
The victim's 22-year-old partner, a Malagasy woman, reportedly inflicted the fatal blows. The event unfolded in front of their two children. The man, a Mahoran, did not survive his injuries.

The woman also suffered minor injuries during the altercation and was taken to the Mayotte Hospital Center for treatment. Upon her release from the hospital, she was placed in police custody at the Koungou gendarmerie station.

km.headline: CAF inspection boosts Comoros' international match hopes at Maluzini stadium
km.dek: An inspection by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) found significant improvements at the Stade de Maluzini, raising prospects for international matches to return.
paragraphs: The Stade de Maluzini in Comoros shows improved conditions following a CAF inspection between August fifteen and nineteen, indicating a potential return of international football. This assessment by a Congolese expert from the continental body yielded more encouraging results than a previous check in mid-2025.

Recent work by the Ministry of Sports, in coordination with the Comorian Football Federation, addressed several areas. The natural turf has a better appearance, though it still requires maintenance adjustments. Anti-slip coatings were installed in corridors and access points to changing rooms and offices, meeting CAF recommendations.

A decision on the stadium's approval is expected around August thirty. Before then, further enhancements are needed, including seat numbering and strengthening the lighting of the playing area. Approval would be a relief for the Coelacanths, who are scheduled to play home matches between September twenty-seven and October six, after an away game in Yaoundé for the CAN 2027 qualifiers.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau votes on constitution expanding presidential powers
gw.dek: Voters in Guinea-Bissau will decide on Sunday whether to adopt a new constitution that grants the president significant new authority, ahead of December elections.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau is preparing for a referendum this Sunday on a proposed constitution that would increase presidential powers and alter the nation's political structure. The changes would allow the president to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and cabinet, create or abolish ministries, and chair the Council of Ministers. The president could also dissolve parliament during a severe political crisis and dismiss the government under specific conditions.

The proposed reforms also include reducing the parliament from 102 seats to 65 and cutting electoral constituencies from 29 to 12. Supporters argue these changes could reshape political institutions, while critics, such as Professor Manuel Nobre de Barros of Lusofona University, warn of an excessive concentration of power in the presidency, potentially giving the president unchecked authority.

This vote occurs less than a year after a military coup, which took place just before presidential election results were to be announced. The new constitution also introduces a requirement for presidential candidates to have resided permanently in Guinea-Bissau for the five years prior to their candidacy. The referendum on August 30 precedes general elections scheduled for December.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau Government launches national literature prize
gw.dek: The Government of Guinea-Bissau, through the Directorate-General for Culture, has initiated the first edition of the “Vasco Cabral” National Literature Prize to encourage.
paragraphs: The Government of Guinea-Bissau launched the first edition of the “Vasco Cabral” National Literature Prize on Tuesday, August twenty-fifth, two thousand twenty-six. This initiative aims to stimulate literary output and promote reading habits across the country. The prize will feature two categories: poetry and short stories, with awards for the top three entries in each.

Edison Ferreira, president of the organizing committee, highlighted Vasco Cabral's significance as an academic, writer, and international peace promoter during the launch ceremony. Ferreira noted that the project, fifteen years in the making, faced financial obstacles before the current government agreed to fully fund this edition.

The prize is part of celebrations marking the centenary of Vasco Cabral's birth, recognizing him as a key intellectual figure in contemporary Guinea-Bissau. Inscriptions for the competition are now open and will close on October ninth, two thousand twenty-six, with regulations available at the Directorate-General for Culture.
